system.summary: Syllabic code of numbers 1 to about 550, one number per letter, syllable, common word or name, with homophones; written as dash- or point-separated numbers inside clear French. Probably the 'chiffre' that reached Baudouin from de Neufville by 30 March 1779; who composed it is not shown.

prior_solution.where: No edition of this correspondence or its code was found. PBF 28:354 n.9 cites the 23 Feb 1779 Baudouin note (p.495) with recipient unknown; the volume's 19th-century index names 'Du Noyer, Bowdoin or Mad. D. Arras'; Butler's 1978 index lists 'Van Temmel'.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling directed the research and set the contribution scope; the work was done with AI agents.

solution.what: Found the free NARA Catalog copy of the file (file unit 464816476, 808 images) and mapped Fold3 page numbers to its frames.
Transcribed de Neufville's enciphered fair draft pp.604-606 twice and aligned it with his plain draft on p.599 (19 April 1779, 'Mad. d'Arras').

Built key K1 (139 numbers) only from his interlined drafts pp.600-603 and 609, froze it, and predicted pp.604-605: 139 of 146 covered groups as in his draft; 200 shuffled keys at most 15. Held-out pairs: 8 of 10, shuffled at most 3.
Key K2 (170 numbers) frozen with the whole 6 May 1779 draft (p.608) held out: 64 of 65 covered groups predicted; 200 shuffled keys at most 7.
Added the recipient's glosses over Baudouin's letters pp.516-548 and 579; full key 204 numbers frozen (key_full_r3.json).

Checked on the leaves the volume's 19th-century index identification 'Du Noyer, Bowdoin or Mad. D. Arras': letters of 23 Feb and 7 Mar 1779 signed 'Baudouin', the second saying he will in future sign a name from the enclosed little cipher (and that he is making a cipher); same hand later signs 'Dunoyer'.
Read the bare groups of pp.491-492 and 573 with the frozen key; two unglossed lines of p.527 decoded but not read.

Searched Founders Online, HathiTrust full text (incl. search-only Schulte Nordholt and van Winter), Cryptiana and the repository: PBF 28:354 n.9 cites the 23 Feb 1779 Baudouin note (recipient unknown); nothing prints the letters' text, content or code.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 305 tokens, 119 types, fr-1750-nospace order 4: reading -2.099 per letter; random keys -3.504 (z 9.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.188 (mean -2.219, z 4.1); annealer on the real text -2.077. Verdict: pass.

A second AI agent of ours took 183 pairs from drafts pp.599 and 601 before seeing the key (87 of 94 numbers agree), confirmed 38 of 39 further entries on the images and reran the three tests identically. Its corrections (224 m/n, 381 is 384, 9 deux/da, 71 on/mme) are checked on the images and kept in key/corrections_post_test.tsv; the frozen keys are unchanged; no reading changes.

Integration check of PR #587. The three tests rerun from the pair files: T1 139 of 146 (shuffles max 15 of 200), T2 8 of 10 (max 3), T3 64 of 65 (max 7); the three key hashes equal key/FREEZE.txt. Own T1 with 2,000 shuffles: mean 1.8, max 23; 139 is 77.7% of all 179 groups with a draft unit (33 are not covered by K1). An independent decoder built from the pair files gives the same 204-number key and the same decodes of B573, B491, B492 and B527; one difference: 136 has one vote each for 'a' (accented) and 'au', the frozen key holds the first, the decode file prints 'au'. Images fetched from the National Archives Catalog (frames 0428, 0363, 0364a, 0449, 0450, 0455b, 0365-0371, 0007): all 68 numbers of the three bare passages agree with the transcription (the last number of p.573 looks like 369); about 60 of the 69 p.608 pairs, 35 p.600 pairs and 40 p.599 pairs were compared and agree. The p.608 truth file leaves out at least 13 groups that stand on the page (313 in 'connoisse', 32 290 85 60, 204 before 'envie', 261 310 133, 88 74 61 230 248 164), so T3 scores the pairs the transcriber aligned, not the whole page. On p.599 the number 30 stands over 're' in 'encore', so 'g' for 30 in B573 and B492 is against the key and is counted as a hole. The index entry (p.3), the signatures 'Baudouin' of 23 February and 7 March 1779, the sentence about the 'petit chiffre' and the cover to 'Van Temmel' were seen on the images. Founders Online returned an empty response to scripted requests, so the Franklin Papers notes were not checked here. Strict word shares: B573 13 of 18, B491 10 of 16, B492 1 of 4.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.037; polyphony 0.036; 29 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.077

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The writer's own plain drafts with numbers written over them, and the recipient's glosses, give the code; a key frozen from some drafts predicts the others.

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: free images located, the code reconstructed from de Neufville's drafts and tested on held-out drafts, the leaf evidence for the index's identification of 'Dunoyer' as Baudouin, and the bare passages of pp.491-492 and 573 read. Checked by a second AI agent of ours, not by a person.
Jean de Neufville, who wrote the code numbers over his own drafts (who composed the code is not shown), and glossed some of Baudouin's letters; Baudouin, who read de Neufville's letters in it.
The Department of State clerk who indexed the volume (p.3): 'Du Noyer, Bowdoin or Mad. D. Arras'.

texts.label: B573, Dunoyer (Baudouin) to de Neufville, 24 January 1780
texts.summary: The patriarch and the merry band will make [them] swallow the last pill, to the shame of the States General; [3] long ago took 'the loan business' away from the [?]rands and gave it up; a loan nobody will put money into can only harm the credit of [369/349]; speak to 'M. du Fresne' (Chaumont). That the loan is the American loan is inference.
texts.note: Strict count at integration (14 Nov 2026), in words carried by code numbers: 13 of 18 = 72%. Holes: [3], [58]rands, [227]er, ar{g}ent (30 is 're' in the key; 'g' is set by the word) and the last number (369 or 349). The contributor's figure, counted in numbers with a key value: 39 of 43 = 91%.

reading_review.note: Code groups decoded with the frozen key and read in the clear French of the letter; holes kept; not rechecked by a second agent. A second AI agent of ours retranscribed p.573 and p.491 independently and agreed group for group except the last number of p.573.

outcome.notes: Most coded text in the file was read at the time: de Neufville's drafts carry his plain French, and he glossed many of Baudouin's letters. The volume's own 19th-century index identifies Du Noyer as Baudouin. What is new is the reconstruction of the code from the drafts, the leaf evidence for that identification, and the reading of the bare passages. PBF 28:354 n.9 cites one Baudouin letter of the file.
